extraFacts.fact: A muffler or silencer on the exhaust port of a pneumatic valve or cylinder reduces the noise of exhausting air and keeps dirt out of the port; a muffler that is too small or clogged adds back pressure and slows the cylinder, so it must be sized to the exhaust port and the flow. A speed control muffler adds an adjustable needle so the exhaust flow, and with it the cylinder speed, can be set.
extraFacts.source: Indus Hydraulics guide 'Push-to-connect fittings and silencers'; maker silencer catalogues

extraFacts.fact: Push-to-connect (push-in) fittings join tube without tools: the tube is pushed in to a collet that grips it, and a release ring is pressed to remove it. The tube must be cut square and be the right outside diameter.
extraFacts.source: Indus Hydraulics guide 'Push-to-connect fittings and silencers'

extraFacts.fact: Unit conversions: 1 bar = 14.5038 psi, so 12 psi is about 0.8 bar, 232 psi is 16 bar and 300 psi is about 21 bar; 25.4 mm = 1 inch, so 12.70 mm is 1/2 inch, 22.22 mm is 7/8 inch and 38.10 mm is 1-1/2 inch; 1 cfm = 28.3 litres per minute. Temperature: deg C = (deg F - 32) / 1.8, so +36 deg F is about 2 deg C, +122 deg F is 50 deg C and 140 deg F is 60 deg C.

Customs classification: taps, cocks and valves fall under HS heading 8481; filtering or purifying machinery parts under 8421; tube or pipe fittings of copper under 7412 and base-metal mountings and brackets under 8302. The headings on the Transair listings differ from each other.
extraFacts.source: WCO Harmonized System Nomenclature 2022, headings 84.81, 84.21, 74.12 and 83.02

extraFacts.fact: Sibling listings on indushydraulics.com: Dixon conical mufflers run 1/8 to 1 inch (CMF18 to CMF88) at 300 psi; Dixon speed control mufflers SCM18 to SCM88 run from 20 scfm to 100 scfm at 300 psi; Texas Pneumatic Tools exhaust mufflers ASP-1 to ASP-12 run 1/8 to 1-1/2 inch, silencer mufflers ASQF run 1/4 to 2 inch (FPT and MPT) and speed control mufflers ASP-1SC to ASP-8SC run 1/8 to 1 inch; Parker EM sintered bronze mufflers have hex sizes 5/16 to 2 inch and Parker EM flow-control mufflers 1/2 to 1-5/16 inch hex; Wilkerson XMC silencers have 1/2, 1 and 1-1/2 inch ports with 12 psi; Transair fittings are for 12.70, 22.22, 25 and 38.10 mm tube.
extraFacts.source: Indus Hydraulics product listings compiled from the maker catalogues

faqs.q: What are Dixon conical mufflers used for?
faqs.a: Dixon conical mufflers are small steel exhaust mufflers screwed into the exhaust port of a pneumatic valve or cylinder to cut noise. This listing carries 6 part numbers, CMF18 to CMF88, in sizes from 1/8" to 1" with a 300 psi stated rating.

faqs.q: How do I read Dixon part numbers such as CMF38 and CMF68?
faqs.a: In the rows the digit before the final 8 is the size in eighths of an inch: CMF18 is 1/8", CMF28 1/4", CMF38 3/8", CMF48 1/2", CMF68 3/4" and CMF88 1". The overall lengths run from 1-1/8" to 2-7/8".

faqs.q: Which sizes do Dixon conical mufflers come in?
How do I choose the right Dixon conical muffler size?
faqs.a: Match the muffler thread to the exhaust port of the valve or cylinder, and go one size up if the port exhausts a large volume, since an undersized muffler slows the cylinder. See our [push-to-connect fittings and silencers guide](/blog/push-to-connect-fittings-and-silencers).

faqs.q: What pressure can a Dixon conical muffler take?
faqs.a: The listing gives a stated pressure of 300 psi, about 21 bar, on all six sizes. For plated steel mufflers, the maker's figure is the only rating on the listing.

faqs.q: What is a Dixon conical muffler made from?
faqs.a: The listing gives steel, with CMF38 and CMF68 described as plated steel conical mufflers. Ask us for corrosion or media requirements before ordering.

faqs.q: Which documents are available for Dixon conical mufflers?
faqs.a: This listing holds no datasheet or certificate file for the Dixon conical mufflers, so name the document you need, for example a certificate of conformity or the Dixon catalogue page for CMF38, and we request it from Dixon with the order.

faqs.q: Which ports do Dixon conical mufflers screw into?
faqs.a: They screw into the exhaust port of a valve, see [solenoid valves and manifolds](/c/pneumatic-solenoid-valves), or a [pneumatic cylinders](/c/pneumatic-cylinders) exhaust. Match the muffler thread to the port, 1/8" to 1".

faqs.q: How do I fit and maintain a Dixon conical muffler?
faqs.a: Screw it into the exhaust port with thread sealant if required, and check it is clear of dirt. Replace a muffler that clogs, as it adds back pressure and slows the cylinder.

faqs.q: How do Dixon conical mufflers differ from Dixon speed control mufflers?
faqs.a: The conical muffler only silences, while the [Dixon speed control muffler](/p/dixon-speed-control-mufflers) also has an adjustable flow control to set cylinder speed.

faqs.q: What are Dixon speed control mufflers used for?
faqs.a: Dixon speed control mufflers are brass mufflers with an adjustable needle that set cylinder speed through the exhaust while silencing it. This listing carries 6 part numbers, SCM18 to SCM88, with adjusted flows of 20 to 100 scfm and a 300 psi stated rating.

faqs.q: How do I read Dixon part numbers such as SCM28 and SCM88?
faqs.a: In the rows the digit before the final 8 is the size in eighths of an inch, matching the Dixon CMF series: SCM18 is 1/8", SCM28 1/4" and SCM88 1". The flow rises with size from 20 scfm (SCM18) to 100 scfm (SCM88).

faqs.q: Which flows do Dixon speed control mufflers offer?
faqs.a: Rows give 20, 30, 40, 60, 70 and 100 scfm maximum adjusted flow, for example SCM18 at 20 scfm and SCM88 at 100 scfm. Pick the size from the exhaust flow of your cylinder.

faqs.q: How big are Dixon speed control mufflers?
faqs.a: Rows give heights from 1-5/16" (the 20 scfm SCM18) to 2-1/2" (the 100 scfm SCM88), including 1-9/16", 1-5/8", 2" and 2-3/8" on the middle sizes.

faqs.q: What pressure can a Dixon speed control muffler take?
faqs.a: The listing gives a stated pressure of 300 psi, about 21 bar, on all six. Use it only on the exhaust port, where the pressure is low, as the muffler is not a pressure regulator.

faqs.q: What is a Dixon speed control muffler made from?
faqs.a: The listing gives brass. Brass suits compressed-air exhaust; ask us before using it in corrosive atmospheres. Send the medium and operating conditions with your enquiry and we confirm material suitability with the maker.

faqs.q: Where do Dixon speed control mufflers fit?
faqs.a: In the exhaust port of a valve or cylinder, see [solenoid valves and manifolds](/c/pneumatic-solenoid-valves) and [pneumatic cylinders](/c/pneumatic-cylinders). For inline speed control see the [flow controls, check and quick exhaust valves](/c/pneumatic-flow-check-valves).

faqs.a: Screw it into the exhaust port, open the needle, then close it gradually until the cylinder reaches the speed you need. Lock the setting. See our [push-to-connect fittings and silencers guide](/blog/push-to-connect-fittings-and-silencers).
